paper.title: Learning Game-Playing Agents with Generative Code Optimization
paper.central_claim: Generative optimization of modular Python game policies using execution traces and natural-language feedback achieves competitive Atari long-horizon sparse-reward performance with significantly less training time and fewer interactions than deep RL, while remaining interpretable and adaptable.

provenance.notes: Configured sonnet → gpt-6.1-sol; provider-verified model/session receipt unavailable, null rather than invented. Segmented continuation; prior completed two outputs not read.

evidence.support_explanation: Existing Trace/OptoPrime machinery extended to Atari rather than newly invented graph optimizer.
LLM policy consumes privileged compact object representations; not raw-pixel learning.

evidence.quote: for each game, we instantiate custom planning and acting components
evidence.support_explanation: Game-specific human scaffold includes trajectories, brick tunnel strategy and movement/shooting decomposition.
Each update takes short traced rollout plus long episode reward; same-game feedback used to revise code.

evidence.quote: we cap rollouts at 400 steps for Pong, 300 for Breakout, and 15 for Space Invaders.
evidence.support_explanation: Trace context bounds substantially shorter than roughly4000-step feedback evaluation.

evidence.quote: the user defines the high-level function interfaces, writes docstrings and starter code, and configures automatic feedback.
evidence.support_explanation: Human prior contribution not limited to neutral observation; final policy updated autonomously after setup.

evidence.quote: we evaluate the performance of the agent with longer evaluation rollouts and use that reward as feedback to the generative optimizer
evidence.support_explanation: Full-game evaluation is training/selection feedback, not independent test.

evidence.quote: RL algorithms are trained with 8 parallel environment instances, while our agent uses only 1.
evidence.support_explanation: Reported timing not matched input/parallelism/hardware training comparison.
Efficient32-environment RL Breakout result challenges blanket time dominance; authors disclose.

evidence.quote: Final policies are consistently more complex than initial scaffold
evidence.support_explanation: Initial/best policies persisted and reused; more code/complexity not independent interpretable/correctness certificate.

evidence.quote: incorporating full-game evaluation reward as feedback
evidence.support_explanation: Pong7→21 ablation bundles longer-horizon reward with staged language, not isolated graph credit or staging.

evidence.quote: LLMs can introduce occasional unstable edits and the performance depends on carefully crafted prompts
evidence.support_explanation: Negative behavior and human prompt sensitivity acknowledged; no rollback/admission safeguard specified.

evidence.quote: Runtime is computed from the Weights & Biases log.
evidence.support_explanation: External baseline times sourced from standardized public logs, not our reproduction; different termination rules.

evidence.quote: For Breakout and Space Invaders, we reported the full training duration; for Pong, the RL policy plateaued before the experiment finished
evidence.support_explanation: Different RL stopping rules disclosed; no same-target-quality compute curve or total agent optimizer tokens.
Full learned rollout policy supplied: wall reflections, capped bounce loop, adaptive deadzone. Static reading only; not executed.

evidence.quote: Best Learned Policy for Space Invaders (Part 1).

signatures.object: Modular persistent Python policy; trainable trajectory/paddle or shoot/move functions
signatures.information: OCAtari object x/y/w/h/dx/dy observations; human game-specific docstrings/scaffold; short raw execution trajectory, current source and reward-conditioned natural language.
signatures.operation: Initialize human scaffold, trace a short rollout, run approximately4000-step evaluation episode, generate staged feedback, backward from final traced observation and call OptoPrime step to replace annotated code; reuse resulting policy next iteration.
signatures.output: Rewritten program functions and game-specific final policy (AppendixF initial/best snapshots).
signatures.conditions: Readable object states and substantial game interfaces/strategy hints; enough context for short traces; stable code execution.
signatures.feedback: Actual game reward from long evaluation plus hand-written performance-bin language and traced state transitions.
signatures.selection_rule: Iterative optimizer updates for20 configured iterations; best code/stage reported; exact promotion/rollback/no-regression threshold not specified.
signatures.selection_data: Same three Atari games; full-game evaluation reward explicitly flows into proposer.
signatures.persistence: Policy source changes live beyond any one action/episode and run next rollout; optimizer memory size5.
signatures.later_use: Revised functions choose next episodes actions without re-training LLM or RL network.
signatures.claimed_effect: Competitive scores with fewer interactions and lower training wall time; interpretable explicit code.
signatures.failure_boundary: Prompt dependence, unstable edits; short trace/long reward mismatch; no held-back certification, scope beyond game-specific starter templates absent.

gap.author_gap: Neural RL costs millions of interactions and hides policy logic; sparse reward and nondifferentiable code make naïve prompting/search weak for long-horizon game control.
gap.checked_gap: Concrete context-horizon mismatch and inspectable code-policy representation; Trace/OptoPrime already supply graph-based optimization. Main extension is longer Atari episodes with domain scaffold and staged long-game feedback, not novel general code optimizer.
gap.residue: Use bounded trace contexts to improve an explicit program on much longer reward episodes.
gap.stakes: Human-readable sequential controllers without neural policy training; actual end-to-end cost and information advantage matter.
gap.method_response: Per-game annotated functions plus short traced rollout and full-game staged feedback passed to unchanged OptoPrime.
gap.remaining_gap: Mechanistic attribution improvement beyond application; human priors and object-state privilege; independent retained testing; strong equal-budget/object-input baselines; complete interaction/token accounting.
unresolved: Request common fixed original Trace/OptoPrime and LangProp texts, and object-input matched RL baseline protocol if novelty/cost adjudication needs exact independent comparison; no external retrieval done.

claims.result_denominator: Table2: agent21/353/1200 at43m/91m/36m; DQN20/302/1383 at606m/1614m/1612m; PPO19/443/939 at144m/188m/339m. PPO beats agent Breakout; DQN and human beat SpaceInvaders.
